summary.headline: Sterling Tools FY26 standalone fasteners EBITDA rose 17.1% to INR111 crore at 15.3% margin, but management flags Q1 FY27 cost pressure and a delayed EV timeline.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 standalone fastener business total income up 11.4% YoY to INR725.9 crore, EBITDA up 17.1% to INR111 crore, and margin of 15.3% versus 14.5%. Profit before exceptional items rose 27.6% to INR74 crore and operating cash flow was INR83.3 crore. A subsidiary-level Q4 loss of INR21 crore was attributed to a bad-debt provision on one bigger customer, which management said is still likely recoverable. The EV business timeline was pushed out by 3 to 5 years and target aspirations deferred by about a year, with SEM expected to return to profitability in FY28 rather than FY27.

financial_highlights.metric: Cash flow from operations, standalone fasteners (FY26)

segments.name: Standalone fasteners (automotive)
segments.commentary: FY26 total income INR725.9 crore, EBITDA INR111 crore at 15.3% margin; management estimates 25-30% domestic automotive fastener share and is net debt free. Business is strongly cash generative.

segments.name: SEM (EV powertrain / power electronics)
segments.commentary: Profitable at EBITDA and PBT through FY25 but loss-making in FY26; management says it will not be profitable in FY27 but expects return to profitability in FY28. OBC and DC/DC lines due for commissioning by end Q2 FY27, commercial supplies from Q3 FY27; more than 28 active customer programs.

segments.name: STML (HVDC contactors and relays)
segments.commentary: Serial commercial production expected from July/August 2026; brand-label supplies already started. Management sizes current Indian HVDC contactor and pre-charge relay market at about INR300 crore, growing to over INR750 crore by end of decade.

guidance_outlook: Fastener FY27 capex around INR75 crore for capacity expansion, operational enhancements and growth programs; all to be commercialised by Q4 FY27.
Management expects fastener growth ahead of the Indian automotive industry in FY27, barring an extreme event such as the West Asia crisis.
Steady-state standalone EBITDA margin expected to be maintained at around 15% plus; short-term pressure expected in Q1 FY27 from steel, energy and chemical inflation.
Hopeful of customer price increases from Q2 FY27 to offset cost inflation; steel is a pass-through with a 1-3 month lag.
SEM not profitable in FY27, expected back to profitability in FY28.
Target of 50% of revenue from non-fastener businesses pushed back due to slower EV penetration.
Railway opportunity not expected to be meaningful revenue for the next 2 years.
Fastener revenue potential about INR800 crore plus with current and FY27 capacity, rising to INR900-1,000 crore with further capex next year; asset turn around 1.8-2x.
capex_capacity: Fastener capex of around INR75 crore in FY27, invested in existing facilities for capacity, balancing and efficiency/quality improvements.
SEM OBC and DC/DC production lines to be commissioned by end of Q2 FY27 (Jaideep said Q3 in one answer); commercial supplies from Q3 FY27.
STML fully automated Bangalore facility for high-voltage components; serial production from July/August 2026.
Asset turn target around 2x (1.8x cited as benchmark) with payback of about 24 months on brownfield capex.
demand_pricing: Indian passenger vehicle sales hit record 46.4 lakh units in FY26, up 7.9%; Q4 FY26 PV sales up 13.2%. 2-wheelers reached 2.17 crore units, up 10.7%.

Management says steel is a straight pass-through with a lag of 1-3 months; energy, chemicals and plastics costs are not covered by norms and are being addressed through price increases and efficiency.
No annual price-reduction contracts with OEMs; prices negotiated on competitive and cost scenarios.
Imports not cheaper than domestic supply per management; localisation by OEMs is a slow, strategic process.
Management estimates e-bus industry could ramp to about 10,000 units a year; onboarded CV customers not yet shown in presentation.
Single-source OBC/DC-DC supply to start with; second source likely once volumes reach scale.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the INR21 crore subsidiary loss in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Jaideep Wadhwa said it was a bad-debt provision on one of the bigger customers, taken prudently even though recovery is considered highly probable; operating PBT is not as severe as it appears.

qa_highlights.question: Are there annual price-reduction contracts with OEMs, and what margin pressure is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul Aggarwal said there are no price-reduction contracts; Q1 FY27 will be a special pressure quarter, with price increases from customers expected from Q2 and efficiency gains to offset.

qa_highlights.question: What is the domestic market share and non-auto revenue exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates 25-30% share of the domestic automotive fastener market; revenue is predominantly automotive. Railway is early-stage and not expected to be meaningful for two years.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors view payback on EV investments that will not yield revenue for 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul said investments are strategic, first-of-kind products for India, value-margin dilutive for a phase; management acknowledged short-term pain in the next 1-2 years but believes in long-term payoff.

qa_highlights.question: When will SEM return to EBITDA and PBT profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Jaideep said SEM will not be profitable in FY27 but there is no reason it cannot be profitable in FY28; other businesses depend on their start-up timelines.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable fastener margin, and will margins moderate near term?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul said there may be short-term pressure, but steady-state EBITDA margin should be maintained around 15% plus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue potential and asset turn on the INR75 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul said capex will be commercialised by Q4 FY27, revenue potential about INR800 crore plus, rising to INR900-1,000 crore; asset turn around 2x, with 24-month turnaround on brownfield capex.

qa_highlights.question: How is vendor selection for OBC and DC/DC supply, and what is the right to win?
qa_highlights.answer: Jaideep said the company starts as 100% single source, with a second source possible at higher volumes. Right to win rests on partner credibility, technical support and multifunction (3-in-1 to 6-in-1) integration capability through GTAKE and Landworld.

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 margin pressure from steel, energy and chemical inflation; pass-through is lagged and energy/chemicals not normed.
Whether OEM price increases from Q2 FY27 materialise as expected.
Continued SEM losses in FY27 and EV penetration remaining below expectations; non-fastener revenue target of 50% pushed back.
Customer credit quality after the INR21 crore subsidiary bad-debt provision.
Commissioning and commercial ramp of OBC/DC-DC lines and STML serial orders from July/August 2026.
Management described the capital allocation for new EV products as value-margin dilutive and capital-intensive.
West Asia crisis effects on crude, commodities, currency and shipping routes.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the core fastener business and long-term EV thesis, but cautious and somewhat defensive on near-term SEM and new-product economics. Management repeatedly acknowledged pain in FY27 and deferred timelines, and some answers on EV revenue and payback were vague.
key_quotes: Short-term, there's a lot of pain like we have seen pain last year and the next year or 2, but we strongly believe in our future.
No, we don't have any price reduction contracts , nowhere. Prices remain constant.
We are confident that we'll be able to mainta in our EBITDA margins around 15% plus.
At least as far as the SEM business is concerned, we expect to be back to profitability next year.
